@facts      order   = [index, submitterKey, side, limitPrice, qtyBase]   side 0 = BID, 1 = ASK

@facts      batchId = the case-level Clearing.batch_id (absent => 0). It is LEAF FIELD 1, so

@facts      ⚠ THE `quote` COLUMN IS THE PUBLISHED quote_sats. On a BID it is the debit (rounded
@facts        UP); on an ASK it is the credit NET of that ask fee — clearing.move stores the

@facts      ⚠ THE `fee` COLUMN IS floor(gross * bps / 10_000) FOR THAT ONE ASK, and it is NOT

cases.name: empty-batch
cases.why: A batch settles every pass, orders or not (aphotic.md §7.3). No orders, no cross, root = 32 zero bytes.

cases.name: all-bids-no-asks
cases.why: supply(p) = 0 at every candidate ⇒ vol(p) = 0 everywhere ⇒ no crossing price.

cases.name: all-asks-no-bids
cases.why: The mirror of all-bids: demand(p) = 0 everywhere.

cases.name: no-cross-bid-below-ask
cases.why: bid 40 < ask 50. At p=40 supply=0; at p=50 demand=0. Both vols are 0.

cases.name: exact-touch-best-bid-equals-best-ask
cases.why: One candidate, 45. demand = supply = 1e6 ⇒ vol 1e6, imbalance 0. quote = 1e6 * 45 = 45_000_000, exact both ways ⇒ no dust.

cases.name: single-crossing-pair-lowest-price-wins
cases.why: Candidates {40, 50}: both give vol 1e6 and imbalance 0. The third tie-break — LOWEST p — picks 40, so the seller's limit sets the price.

cases.name: bid-side-short-ask-is-rationed
cases.why: demand 400_000 < supply 1e6 at every candidate ⇒ matched 400_000, the ASK is the long side and is pro-rated (a single order, so it simply truncates).

cases.name: ask-side-short-bid-is-rationed
cases.why: The mirror. matched = supply = 300_000.

cases.name: every-order-at-the-same-price-full-prorata
cases.why: 3 bids of 100 against 1 ask of 100, all at p*. floor(100*100/300) = 33 each (99); every remainder is 100 so the single leftover unit goes to the FIRST canonical position (A1 < A2 < A3).

cases.name: prorata-remainder-needs-largest-remainder
cases.why: matched 101 over three equal weights of 100: floor = 33 each (99), remainder 200 each, TWO leftover units ⇒ the first two canonical positions get +1.

cases.name: prorata-unequal-weights-largest-remainder-not-first-index
cases.why: Weights 50/30/20, matched 71. floors 35/21/14 = 70; remainders 50/30/20. The one leftover goes to the LARGEST remainder (A1, 50) — which here also happens to be first, so the next case proves the tie path.

cases.name: duplicate-prices-from-one-submitter
cases.why: A1 submits TWO bids at the same price. They are two independent canonical positions, not one aggregated order: 150 over weights 100/100 divides exactly, 75 each.

cases.name: duplicate-price-and-submitter-forces-index-tiebreak
cases.why: Same price AND same submitter ⇒ only the submission index can break the tie. Indices are 5 and 2, so index 2 sorts FIRST and takes the single leftover unit. Submission ORDER in the array is deliberately the reverse of the canonical order.

cases.name: submitter-bytes-tiebreak-outranks-index
cases.why: AHI = 0xff00.. submitted FIRST (index 0), A1 = 0x0000..01 second (index 1). Canonical order is submitter BYTES ascending BEFORE index, so A1 sorts first and takes the leftover unit. Proves the tie-break precedence, and that the comparison is on bytes, not on submission time.

cases.name: price-priority-strictly-inside-fills-fully
cases.why: docs/DESIGN-V2.md §5.3 verbatim: the bid at 12 is STRICTLY inside the cross and fills fully (100); the bid at exactly p*=10 is pro-rated for the 50 residual. Candidate 10 gives vol 150 vs 100 at candidate 12, so max-volume decides the price.

cases.name: degenerate-strictly-inside-exceeds-matched
cases.why: THE case §5.3 leaves undefined. bid 100@10 vs ask 50@5: both candidates give vol 50 and imbalance 50, so the LOWEST price wins and p*=5 — which makes the whole bid strictly inside the cross while matched is only 50. The generalisation pro-rates the first level that does not fit. Pin this or the two implementations will disagree the first time it happens.

cases.name: three-level-book-max-volume-wins
cases.why: Candidates 10/11/12 give vol 100/200/100. Max volume picks 11 outright — no tie-break needed. Both 12-bids and 11-bids fill fully; the 10-bid and the 12-ask are outside the cross and get nothing.

cases.name: imbalance-tiebreak-beats-lowest-price
cases.why: Candidate 8 → demand 300 / supply 100 → vol 100, |gap| 200. Candidate 10 → demand 100 / supply 200 → vol 100, |gap| 100. Equal volume, so the SECOND tie-break decides and picks 10 — the lowest-price rule never gets a vote. Also shows ask-side price priority: the 8-ask fills fully and the 10-ask gets nothing.

cases.name: full-tie-picks-lowest-price
cases.why: bid 100@12 vs ask 100@8. Both candidates give vol 100 and imbalance 0 — a complete tie all the way down. The third rule picks 8.

cases.name: fee-30-bps-on-a-single-fill
cases.why: One ask, gross 40_000_000. Move charges THAT ask floor(40_000_000*30/10_000) = 120_000 and publishes the NET 39_880_000 in the leaf; the buyer still debits the full 40_000_000. fee_quote = quote_paid - quote_recv = 120_000, with no dust to absorb.

cases.name: fee-charged-per-ask-on-its-own-gross
cases.why: Move charges each ask individually: floor(1000*33/10_000) = 3 and floor(2500*33/10_000) = 8, published NET as 997 and 2492. Sum 11. The old spec computed ONE floor(3500*33/10_000) = 11 apportioned by largest remainder, which happened to give 3/8 too — the totals coincide here and the per-ask rule is what is pinned.

cases.name: fee-at-the-10000-bps-boundary
cases.why: The maximum legal fee takes the whole gross, so the ask publishes a quote_sats of exactly 0 and is never negative. settle_step skips a zero credit, so the boundary is also the only case where an ask fill moves no quote at all.

cases.name: fee-zero-bps
cases.why: The same book with no fee — the control for the two cases above.

cases.name: batch-id-is-committed-to-the-leaf
cases.why: Byte-for-byte the fee-zero-bps book, cleared under batch_id 7. Every scalar and every fill row is identical; only the ROOT may differ, because batch_id is the FIRST field of bcs(Fill). If the two roots ever match, the leaf has stopped committing to the batch.

cases.name: rounding-toward-the-vault-creates-dust
cases.why: price 1 and qty 1.5e9 make the exact quote 1.5. The bid rounds UP to 2, the ask DOWN to 1. Move credits the 1-unit residual to the FEE RECIPIENT as part of fee_quote = quote_paid - quote_recv — there is no separate dust credit on chain, which is why feeQuote is 1 at ZERO bps.

cases.name: dust-across-multiple-fills-with-a-zero-fee-base
cases.why: Splitting the ask in two makes BOTH ask quotes floor to 0 while the bid still pays 2 — matchedQuote 0, dust 2, and fee_quote = 2 - 0 = 2 at zero bps. The fee base can legitimately be 0 on a non-empty match.

cases.name: underfunded-bid-truncates-both-sides
cases.why: A1 froze only 10_000_000 quote, which at p*=50 buys 200_000 base. The ask is then recomputed SYMMETRICALLY down to the same 200_000 — no margin field ever existed, so solvency is resolved at settlement without leaking size at submit.

cases.name: underfunded-ask-truncates-both-sides
cases.why: The mirror: the seller froze only 300_000 base, so the fully-funded buyer is cut to 300_000 too.

cases.name: underfunded-account-with-two-orders-canonical-priority
cases.why: A1 has 150 base but two asks of 100. The budget is consumed in CANONICAL order, so index 1 gets 100 and index 2 gets the remaining 50 — not 75/75. The bid is then re-rationed from 200 down to 150.

cases.name: zero-frozen-balance-yields-no-fills
cases.why: A crossing price EXISTS (cleared = true, price recorded) but nothing settles. `matchedBaseBeforeTruncation` keeps the pre-truncation volume so the transparency surface can say how much solvency cost the batch. Empty fills ⇒ root = 32 zero bytes.

cases.name: missing-balance-entry-is-treated-as-zero
cases.why: A1 is absent from the frozen snapshot entirely. Fail CLOSED — an unknown account has nothing, never everything.

cases.name: balances-absent-disables-truncation
cases.why: The same book with NO frozen snapshot at all clears in full. Distinguishes 'no ledger supplied' from 'a ledger of zeros' — the previous two cases are the second.

cases.name: u64-boundary-quantity-on-one-side
cases.why: A bid of u64::MAX against an ask of 1000; matched is 1000. ceil(1000/1e9) = 1 vs floor = 0, so the whole quote leg is the 1-unit dust, and fee_quote = 1 - 0 = 1 at zero bps.

cases.name: u64-boundary-quantity-both-sides-exact-fit
cases.why: u64::MAX base at price exactly 1e9 makes the quote u64::MAX too — the largest batch that can settle at all. Nothing overflows, nothing rounds.

cases.name: u64-boundary-quantity-both-sides-quote-overflows
cases.why: One tick above the exact-fit case the quote no longer fits a u64 Balance. Move aborts inside ceil_mul_div (EOverflow) on the FIRST fill it roots, not on a sum — so the guard that fires is the per-fill one.

cases.name: u128-price-rejected-move-holds-a-u64
cases.why: This case used to assert that a u128 price round-trips through discovery. It does not exist on chain: aphotic::clearing holds limit_price in a u64, so a u128 price is rejected at validation rather than accepted into a book the settlement layer cannot represent.

cases.name: u64-max-price-with-quantity-overflows-the-quote
cases.why: With a u64 price the quote can still leave u64 — it just needs quantity too: 2e9 base at u64::MAX / 1e9 is 3.689e19 > u64::MAX. Move aborts inside floor_mul_div (EOverflow); here the per-fill guard fires with the same effect.

cases.name: u64-max-price-still-settles-a-single-unit
cases.why: u64::MAX / 1e9 = 18_446_744_073.709…, so one base unit settles: the bid ceils to 18_446_744_074 and the ask floors to 18_446_744_073. The largest price the deployed contract can hold, and it pins the ceil/floor asymmetry at the very top of the u64 range — dust 1, credited to the fee recipient at zero bps.

cases.name: same-submitter-on-both-sides
cases.why: A1 is both a buyer and a seller in one batch — legal, and it must not net internally. The 9-ask fills fully by price priority, then A1's own 10-ask takes the 50 residual.

cases.name: batch-256-single-price-level
cases.why: MAX_BATCH_SIZE exactly (docs/DESIGN-V2.md D4). 128 bids and 128 asks of 100 at one price: demand == supply == 12800, everything fills fully, 256 fills == the max_num_event_emit budget of 257 events with BatchSettled.

cases.name: batch-256-two-price-levels
cases.why: The same size across two levels per side (bids 12/10, asks 8/10). Candidate 10 gives vol 12800 against 6400 at either extreme, so everything still fills — but the canonical sort now has to interleave 128 distinct submitters across two levels.

cases.name: batch-hard-max-512-accepted
cases.why: HARD_MAX_BATCH_SIZE (docs/DESIGN-V2.md D4). 512 orders is the ceiling the setter asserts; it must clear, not abort.

cases.name: over-hard-max-513-rejected
cases.why: One order past the ceiling. The object-size and event walls of docs/DESIGN-V2.md §2 are real; refusing is the only safe answer.

cases.name: duplicate-order-index-rejected
cases.why: The submission index IS the final canonical tie-break, so a duplicate would make the order ambiguous. Reject at the door.

cases.name: zero-quantity-rejected
cases.why: A zero-quantity order carries no information and would appear as a phantom canonical position.

cases.name: zero-price-rejected
cases.why: Price 0 would make the affordability division in the truncation pass divide by zero.

cases.name: fee-bps-above-the-denominator-rejected
cases.why: 10_001 bps would make the fee exceed the matched quote and drive an ask's net credit negative.
